html:
The Soviet occupation of Bessarabia began on 28 June 1940, when Romania gave in to a Soviet ultimatum and handed over Bessarabia and Northern Bukovina without a fight.

The secret protocol of the Molotov Ribbentrop Pact had given the region to the Soviet sphere. Moscow created the Moldavian Soviet Socialist Republic, joining most of Bessarabia to a strip east of the Dniester, and gave the south and north to Ukraine. Romania retook the region with Germany in 1941, and the Soviets returned in 1944. Mass deportations to Siberia and Kazakhstan followed in 1941 and 1949, and famine in 1946 and 1947. The Moldovan state today rests on the borders drawn in 1940.
sum: The Soviet occupation of Bessarabia began on 28 June 1940, when Romania gave in to a Soviet ultimatum and handed over Bessarabia and Northern Bukovina without a fight.
